scope: Evaluate the newly surfaced C++/GGUF runtime path for Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-TTS as a non-duplicate runtime/dependency-consolidation candidate for Frankenstein 2.0 local German voice. Pin upstream evidence, falsify unsupported single-instance memory-sharing assumptions, and define a target A/B handoff. This claim does not overlap T7-SYS-002 hardware-inventory execution and grants no model/runtime/voice acceptance credit by itself.
main_result: CrispASR is a high-value common C++/ggml/GGUF deployment-substrate challenger, but audited server/concurrency semantics do not support the stronger assumption that ASR and TTS share one simultaneously resident model instance or automatically reduce combined model memory.
counterhypothesis_result: FALSIFIED_AT_SOURCE_SCOPE: default server uses one loaded model with serialized inference; multiple workers own independent model instances and cost multiplied model memory. Duplex ASR+TTS must therefore be measured as separate resident instances unless a distinct multi-model loader is proven.
asr_delta: First compact Qwen3-ASR falsifier should preserve the audio tower at Q8_0 according to the audited rebaked GGUF path rather than naively quantizing all tensors to Q4; upstream reports long-audio drift/repetition from sub-Q8 audio-encoder quantization.
parallel_claim_exclusion: T7-SYS-002 remains sole owner of VPS bridge roundtrip + hardware inventory
next_gate: After T7-SYS-002 produces a real hardware receipt, benchmark pinned CrispASR versus official/reference Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-TTS paths on identical German fixtures, then run both speech directions resident concurrently and measure combined RSS/VRAM plus p50/p95/p99 and cancellation correctness.
